scope: Canonical mass-action endpoint normalization, finite-cut sensitivity terms, all-thermal bolt-tip allowance and complete local flat thermal restoration; not the full angular or metric operator.
ordinary_argument_review: Factor the true regular Frobenius branch with a mass-independent leading norm. The explicit flat-polar Bessel normalization depends on mass; dropping it changes the gradient by 2j times the bolt direction and produces a nonsummable error.

The exact rotated action difference has vanishing lower endpoint variation only at the true bolt. At a finite cut, retain positive ell*Y and ell*Z boundary terms in addition to the separately bounded tip integral.

The lowest half-integer thermal channel is resonant for the auxiliary action adjoint: rho log rho appears but its product with a regular sensitivity still vanishes. This auxiliary function is not the gravitational point-source adjoint.

The one-sided mass cubic and weight-four log phase provide the continuous first derivatives needed by the finite-mode transfer. This does not upgrade their reflected regularity or certify the angular parametrix.

Uniform cap barriers use the actual smooth bolt geometry, M epsilon<=.001 and unit direction/epsilon-derivative bounds. The 3100 coefficient and exact sum 6-pi^2/2 give an all-thermal cap, before angular weights.
The actual finite-seed factorization encloses a/rho and a proper derivative on the full chi interval [0,.001], retaining the current positive-temperature h box.

Restore the nonzero-winding local flat thermal term using shifted Gaussian Poisson summation before the proper-time integral. Do not directly apply the Abel-Plana formula at its branch singularities or assign a value to a divergent unregulated sum.

The Gaussian and its second derivative meet DLMF 1.8.14 hypotheses. Positive-real K integrals meet their phase conditions, and the absolute integrated winding series converges at each positive mass-radius y, justifying interchange and mass derivatives.

Near zero, the half-integer finite part fixes the Euler/log constant. Its convergent binomial series and explicit geometric derivative tails overlap the alternating Bessel algorithm. The mass-independent -1/(12a) term remains in the metric/Weyl restoration.

The independently evaluated Fermi integrals and flat-polar Bessel action are diagnostics. The analytic tails and ordinary endpoint comparison supply continuum coverage; checker counts do not establish a full physical solution.

Retain the failed snapshot and numerical record, increase the diagnostic endpoint to exponent 160, and replay the entire package. No analytical bound or target changes.

The fixed-cap upper allowance grows as M_n^2 and cannot be summed with angular degeneracy; its small-cap hypothesis also eventually fails. This rejects that uniform certificate and selects matched bolt/angular cancellation, not nonexistence or a new scheme.
